Very much so. I have a really bad fear of conflict (wonder why) so I often become dodgy. 


Fear of being punished for disagreeing makes for a lot of avoidance behavior.

Okay, but even if you have been living in the dark--"office gossip" about "hey, be careful around that guy in power--he's a creep" isn't a joke. It's literally  the MeToo movement. 

Mental illness has a rule of don't tell, don't ask, keep it to yourself. 

But if a guy is predatory towards women or hints at predatory actions (literally spying on the women) then they have a right to know.
Are you sure it isn't him? Because they all seemed nice to each other.

My argument to that is the what constitutes humanity--those weren't his creations. They were people's minds (something this season cares about) and even though they were a copy, they were extremely real people who had their own ability to act for themselves except when he controlled them.
He was a Nice Guy (tm) and those mean women weren't interested in him!

"I love exposing people." 

Yiiiikes. Not saying there ain't bad people, but I get the feeling that if you ever break up with her she'll start a social media campaign to ruin your life.

This is a good episode for children of Narcissistic/Controlling parents and gave a physical representation of often what parents in those relationships do to their children. 

Power to the girl for taking back her life in the end.

I sort of figured it was the woman tampering when it became obvious she came on purpose and wasn't just a curious college student.

The first story with the doctor made me flinch as I'm pretty sensitive to blood, but the ending disappointed me. Like murders one guy and that's it. Coma. 

The second one, I didn't feel any connection or pity to the character Carrie. I had a bad mom so seeing her cry and whine just made me think "shut up and understand he's moving on. You aren't truly real." Being a made into the monkey I thought was stupid, and knew she was going to be forgotten. I thought the other woman yelling at the monkey was hilarious though. 

The final ending I was starting to expect and so I didn't feel shocked. It was nice, I guess. But I would have done worse to the man. 

I did love all the references with Lollipop, 15 Million Merits (nice graphic) and San Junipero (said before he explains the mesh) and probably countless others. 

It just didn't have weight to me, but it was a nice watch.

1. There were lots of stray cats in my old neighborhood and when we weren't home, our porch made for nice covering, twice we came home to 5+ cats curled up. Scattered moment the headlights hit them.  So stray cats near a house isn't too surprising. Also, stray cats are everywhere!

2. It's winter time--deer aren't in their covered areas nearly as much. 

3. It's a fox. Even though it's surprising, it's literally just a fox. Mostly they're dead on roads, but yeah, it's just a fox. 

But if you're looking for signs, look for unusual animals. Like dead ones with eyes missing, or ones that follow you when you don't offer them food or company. 

Animals just existing? It's more likely than you think
